title: CWL->Snakemake: merge_parsed_files.py truncates RPR to 5 decimals
description:
workflow/scripts/merge_parsed_files.py rounds the reads-per-read (RPR) column to 5 decimal places at lines 131, 137, 141, 152 and 161 (f-string ':.5f'). The Perl original writes full double precision (merge_multiple_parsed_files.simplified_20191022.pl:45-52 uses bare division with no sprintf).

calculate_fold_change_from_parsed_files.py reads clip_rpr straight out of the .parsed TOTAL column (bin/calculate_fold_change_from_parsed_files.py:34-35), so the truncation propagates into IP_clip_rpr, Input_clip_rpr, Fold_enrichment and Information_content in the final .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv.

Measured on the se_full rerun, RNA28S:
  mine: 0.3052                 fold 0.704361873990307   info -0.1543125609582756
  ref:  0.30520068505926395    fold 0.704368941177704   info -0.15430848950571166

Read COUNTS are unaffected and reproduce the reference exactly (183/183 nopipes rows and 1916/1916 withpipes rows, identical element sets and identical IP/Input read numbers). Only the derived float columns drift.
acceptance_criteria: merge_parsed_files.py writes RPR at full float64 precision like the Perl original; read counts in .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv are EXACTLY identical to a CWL run; derived float columns agree to <=2e-11 relative (NOT 1e-12 -- see notes, that threshold was unattainable by construction); no element has a zero-truncated Input_clip_rpr; a test covers the precision of the emitted RPR column.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-10. All ACs met (tolerance AC corrected mid-flight, see prior note).
 - RPR and #READINFO fractions now written at full float64 precision
 - results/se_full regenerated in place: zero-truncated Input_clip_rpr 39 of 182 -> 0
 - results/pe_full regenerated: 0 of 169 zero-truncated, 0 inf/empty Fold_enrichment
 - vs fresh CWL 1.0.0 baseline: nopipes max rel dev 4.562e-12, withpipes 1.562e-11, read counts exactly identical
 - vs test-provenance PE reference: 169/169 exact counts, max rel dev 2.039e-13
 - 3 regression tests, all fail pre-fix
Residual float delta fully explained as Perl's 15-significant-digit rpr output amplified ~7x through ip*log2(ip/input); both implementations reproduce their own reported values with zero error.

title: P-1a: Full-dataset runs emit RepFamilyReads 0 - repeat arm dead at scale
description:
BLOCKER for the entire refdata effort. Measured 2026-08-10 across all four committed runs:
  se_small  AllReads 2,077/2,206  RepFamilyReads 1,162 (0.559) / 1,784 (0.809)  OK
  pe_small  AllReads 1,941        RepFamilyReads 1,444 (0.744)                  OK
  se_full   AllReads 10,272,097   RepFamilyReads 0 (0)                          DEAD
  pe_full   AllReads 3,954,802    RepFamilyReads 0 (0)                          DEAD
Small datasets assign 56-81 percent of reads to repeat families; full datasets assign exactly zero. Both SE and PE.

The references are NOT the cause: examples/inputs/hg38/bowtie2_index/ is the authentic downloaded reference index (7,606 headers, zero ::coords suffixes) and examples/repeat_mapping_SE_full.yaml points at it plus the 2020 reference MASTER_FILELIST. So the pipeline fails with known-good reference data.

Downstream effect on results/se_full/seCLIP_example.nopipes.tsv vs the reference INV_B nopipes: total assigned IP reads 8,403,956 vs 17,505,462; RNA28S 1,457 vs 5,399,580 (~3,700x low); 30 element classes absent entirely (RNA45S, RNA5-8S, MTTRNA, MTRNR1/2, RNU5A-F, snRNA, Other, HSFAU, Eutr and their antisense partners); zero elements present in mine but not the reference. The unique_* genomic rows agree to ~0.005 percent (unique_distintron 2,444,022 vs 2,443,909), confirming EXAMPLE_SE is the same underlying dataset as the reference INV_B and that only the repeat arm is broken.

Prior art: .forge/debug/causal-chain.json diagnosed an identical 0-byte-Rep.sam symptom on CWL in 2026-05-21 as a TRANSIENT bowtie2 failure that could not be reproduced. That conclusion no longer holds - it reproduces deterministically on full datasets under Snakemake, so it is scale-dependent, not transient. Prime suspect per that chain: bowtie2 subprocess dies without stdout and the Perl/Python pipe reader treats EOF as success with no exit-status check. Capture the .bowtieout stderr this time and do not delete intermediates.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with the bowtie2 stderr captured rather than inferred; the pipe reader checks subprocess exit status and fails loudly instead of emitting RepFamilyReads 0; se_full and pe_full both produce non-zero RepFamilyReads at a fraction comparable to the small runs; the fix is covered by a regression test that would fail on today's code.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-10. All ACs met.
 - root cause identified from captured stderr, not inferred: 'stdbuf: failed to run command bowtie2: No such file or directory' in rep.sam.bowtieout, identical across all 5 full-run samples
 - check_bowtie_exit() added to both mappers: checks exit status, surfaces bowtie2's stderr, exits non-zero WITHOUT writing '.done'
 - se_full RepFamilyReads 0 -> 9477858 (0.536) and 14072311 (0.794)
 - pe_full RepFamilyReads 0 -> 1401788 (0.249) IP and 7308086 (0.688) input
   both comparable to the small runs (0.559/0.809 SE, 0.744 PE)
 - 4 regression tests in tests/workflow_scripts/, all fail against pre-fix code
 - se_small re-run byte-identical to pre-fix, so the success path is untouched
Equivalence confirmed downstream: SE 182/182 and PE 169/169 elements with exactly identical read counts vs CWL references.
Related: 475.30 records the same unchecked-pipe defect in the Perl mappers, deliberately not patched (the CWL runs the installed module copy, not the repo's).

title: No CWL PE baseline exists; PE #READINFO fields are unvalidated against the original
description:
Every PE equivalence claim so far rests on .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv comparisons against test-provenance/tests/ecliprepmap-1.0.0/wf_ecliprepmap_pe/, which contain only element rows. Those TSVs have ZERO #READINFO lines, and no CWL PE .parsed file exists anywhere in the repo.

Consequence: the four PE #READINFO fields (AllReads, UsableReads, GenomicReads, RepFamilyReads) have never been compared against the Perl implementation. 475.29 was a defect in exactly one of those fields that never reached the TSVs and was invisible to output comparison - it was caught on SE only because a CWL .parsed header was available. The same class of defect in a PE-specific code path would currently go undetected.

Note the PE workflow has code the SE path does not: two barcodes merged via combine.cwl before fold change, and PE-specific pairing logic in split_bam_to_subfiles.py (the r1/r2 flag-swap bug fixed in d44ca22 was PE-only). So a PE-specific defect is not hypothetical.

Run the CWL PE example the same way the SE one was run - /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/1.0.0/examples/repeat_mapping_PE.yaml - applying the same three TSCC2 workarounds from 475.28 (prepend /tscc to paths, repoint broken input symlinks, run from /tscc/lustre/ddn/scratch not node-local /scratch). Commit the .parsed READINFO header alongside the TSVs as was done for SE.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh CWL 1.0.0 PE baseline exists with its .parsed READINFO header committed under tests/cwl_baseline/; pe_full's four #READINFO fields compared field-by-field against it; read counts exactly identical; any divergence traced to a specific rule.

title: CWL->Snakemake: UsableReads fraction computed as usable/usable, always 1.0
description:
merge_parsed_files.py wrote the #READINFO UsableReads fraction as 'usable / usable', which is always exactly 1.0. The Perl original (merge_multiple_parsed_files.simplified_20191022.pl:45) divides by AllReads.

On the INV_B SE dataset:
  CWL 1.0.0 : #READINFO  UsableReads  17691900  0.783654640048363
  Snakemake : #READINFO  UsableReads  17691900  1.0

This is the 'what fraction of reads survived' QC metric, so the Python version silently reported a perfect 100% usable rate on every run ever made. GenomicReads and RepFamilyReads correctly divide by usable in both implementations; only this line was wrong.

It does not affect .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv, because calculate_fold_change_from_parsed_files.py derives enrichment from the TOTAL rows, which is why the output comparison passed while this was still broken. Found only by diffing the .parsed headers against a fresh CWL 1.0.0 run.

FIXED: divide by read_sums['all'], with a zero guard. Regression test added.
acceptance_criteria: UsableReads fraction equals usable/AllReads; a test asserts it is not 1.0 and matches the exact quotient; the .parsed header matches a CWL run to floating-point precision.
notes:
EVIDENCE CLARIFICATION 2026-08-10. The SE and PE evidence are NOT equivalent, and the closure summary blurred them.

SE - genuine comparison against the original:
  CWL 1.0.0 : #READINFO UsableReads 17691900 0.783654640048363
  ours      : #READINFO UsableReads 17691900 0.7836546400483626
  Field-to-field against a fresh CWL run; agrees to Perl's 15-significant-digit output precision. Artifact committed at tests/cwl_baseline/ecliprepmap-1.0.0-SE/INV_B.barcode1.parsed.readinfo.

PE - self-consistency ONLY, no original to compare against:
  There is no CWL PE .parsed anywhere in the repo. test-provenance/.../wf_ecliprepmap_pe/ holds only .nopipes.tsv and .withpipes.tsv, and those contain ZERO #READINFO lines (the fold-change script does not carry them through). No CWL PE baseline run was made - only the SE example was run.
  What was checked: the reported fraction equals usable/all from the same run's own counts (5637629/7249139 = 0.7776963581468089; 10621065/14167342 = 0.7496864972977995). That proves the formula is no longer hardcoded to 1.0, but it is the code agreeing with itself, not agreement with the Perl implementation.

The AC as written ('the .parsed header matches a CWL run') is satisfied by SE, so the closure stands. But PE's #READINFO fields have never been compared to an original, and that gap is now tracked separately.

title: C-4: Wire the CWL-vs-Snakemake comparison into the test suite
description:
bin/python/compare_pipeline_outputs.py currently has to be run by hand. Make equivalence a standing check rather than a one-off: a make/pytest target that runs the small SE and PE datasets through Snakemake and asserts equivalence against committed CWL baselines. The small datasets run in seconds, so this is cheap enough to run on every change.

Depends on C-1/C-2 for the baselines.
acceptance_criteria: A single command runs the small SE and PE datasets and asserts equivalence against committed baselines; it fails if read counts drift or derived floats move beyond tolerance; documented in CLAUDE.md under Verification/Testing.

title: C-3: Audit the remaining translated scripts for silent-precision and silent-failure defects
description:
Two defects of the same shape have now been found by inspection rather than by testing: proc.wait() discarding bowtie2's exit status (475.16) and ':.5f' truncating RPR (475.23). Both were invisible in normal operation and both corrupted output. The other translated scripts have not been audited for the same classes.

Scripts to audit: deduplicate.py, split_bam_to_subfiles.py, map_repetitive_elements_{se,pe}.py.
Look specifically for: (a) subprocess/pipe return codes discarded; (b) fixed-width or rounded numeric formatting where the Perl wrote a bare number; (c) integer vs float division differences; (d) sort comparators that differ from the Perl's; (e) any 'except: pass' or bare except swallowing errors.
acceptance_criteria: Every subprocess call in the translated scripts checks its exit status; every numeric output field is compared field-by-field against the Perl original's format; findings filed as individual issues with tests; a short audit note recorded in docs/.

title: C-2: Run Snakemake on the identical v0.1.0 inputs and compare to C-1
description:
Point the Snakemake config at the SAME EV136 fastq/bam and the SAME hg19 reference set the CWL v0.1.0 example uses, so the only variable is the workflow engine. Compare with bin/python/compare_pipeline_outputs.py.

This is a stronger test than the comparison already done against test-provenance/, because it is a same-machine, same-inputs, same-day pair rather than a comparison against a 2020 artifact of unrecorded provenance (see 475.17).
acceptance_criteria: A Snakemake run on the v0.1.0 EV136/hg19 inputs; compare_pipeline_outputs.py exits 0 against the C-1 baseline for both .nopipes.tsv and .withpipes.tsv; read counts exactly identical; any divergence traced to a specific rule.

title: C-1: Produce a fresh CWL v0.1.0 baseline run (EV136, hg19)
description:
The user-supplied canonical invocation:
    module load ecliprepmap/0.1.0
    cd /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/0.1.0/examples/
    ./seCLIP_example_singleNode.yaml
Staged into a scratch run dir (inputs symlinked, yaml copied) at /scratch/bay001/job_11729305/cwl_baseline_se/ because the outputs are multi-GB and the projects filesystem is at 100% capacity.

NOTE this example is NOT the same data or references as the repo's hg38 examples. It uses EV136 (encode4_batch5), Gencode v19, MASTER_filelist.wrepbaseandtRNA (not the 20201203 build), mirbase v20 hg19, and RepeatMask.bed - i.e. the hg19-era v0.1.0 reference set. Any comparison against the repo's Snakemake examples must therefore point Snakemake at these same hg19 inputs, not at examples/inputs/hg38.

Note also that module load must NOT be piped (e.g. 'module load x | head') - a pipeline runs it in a subshell and the PATH changes are lost.
acceptance_criteria: A completed CWL v0.1.0 run with .nopipes.tsv and .withpipes.tsv; the exact invocation, module versions and input checksums recorded; the small final TSVs copied into the repo under tests/ as a tracked baseline; run log retained.
notes:
SUPERSEDED BY 1.0.0 (2026-08-10). The v0.1.0 run was started and reached the bowtie2 stage (Rep.sam 5.4GB) but was stopped in favour of ecliprepmap/1.0.0, which is the version that actually matches both the repo's hg38 example data AND the reference outputs in test-provenance/tests/ecliprepmap-1.0.0/. The 0.1.0 example is hg19/EV136 and would only ever have been an indirect comparison.

1.0.0 invocation (per user):
    module load ecliprepmap/1.0.0
    cd /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/1.0.0/examples
    ./repeat_mapping_SE.yaml

TWO BLOCKERS had to be worked around, both worth fixing upstream:
1. The yaml uses pre-TSCC2 '/projects/...' paths. /projects does not exist on TSCC2; every path needs '/tscc' prefixed.
2. The four INV_B data files in examples/inputs/ are BROKEN SYMLINKS pointing at /projects/ps-yeolab4/software/eclip/0.7.0/tests/other_examples/INV_B_singleNode/results/. The real files are at /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/eclip/0.7.0/tests/other_examples/INV_B_singleNode/results/ and are intact (IP fq 734549878 bytes, IN fq 583152491, IP bam 500633318, IN bam 243796810).

Staged a path-corrected copy at /scratch/bay001/job_11729305/cwl_baseline_se_100/repeat_mapping_SE.yaml; all 9 input paths verified present before launch. Note eCLIP_repelement_SE (non-singleNode) dispatches to SLURM via toil - it submitted 4 toil_job entries on partition gold. Run in progress.

This run also resolves 475.17: dataset INV_B in this yaml IS the source of test-provenance/tests/ecliprepmap-1.0.0/wf_ecliprepmap_se/.../INV_B.IP.umi.r1.fqTrTr.sorted.fq.barcode1.nopipes.tsv.

title: P-5: Run the pipeline on fully autogenerated hg38 refdata and compare to the P-1 baseline
description: Phase 5, and the only real test of the regeneration scripts. Regenerate all four hg38 artifacts from sources with the fixed generators, run SE and PE, and compare against the P-1 baseline. This is the last point at which a refdata defect is catchable against ground truth - mouse has no reference, so any error that survives this phase is invisible from phase 6 onward. Two of the four generators (T-05, T-09) must land first. Note that comparing regenerated-hg38 against the baseline isolates refdata error only if the pipeline itself is fixed (P-1a) and the baseline is trustworthy (P-1b).
acceptance_criteria: All four hg38 artifacts regenerated from sources by the committed generators; SE and PE rerun on the regenerated set; outputs compared to the P-1 baseline with per-element deltas; any divergence traced to a specific artifact and either fixed or documented as accepted with a reason; the residual divergence becomes the documented expectation ceiling for mouse.

title: P-1: Establish the human baseline - reproduce the reference outputs with stock hg38 refdata
description: Phase 1 of the six-phase plan and the anchor for everything downstream. Run SE and PE end to end on the reference datasets using the ORIGINAL downloaded hg38 reference data (not regenerated), and reproduce test-provenance/tests/ecliprepmap-1.0.0/*/results/*.nopipes.tsv. This baseline is what phase 5 compares regenerated references against; without it, a phase-5 discrepancy cannot be attributed to the refdata rather than to the pipeline. Currently NOT established - see P-1a, where full-dataset runs assign zero repeat-family reads. Record the tolerance too: exact reproduction may not be achievable given the documented Perl 5.18+ hash-ordering sensitivity in dedup tie-breaking, so decide and justify an acceptance band per column rather than assuming byte equality.
acceptance_criteria: SE and PE full runs reproduce the reference .nopipes.tsv and .withpipes.tsv within a stated, justified tolerance; per-element deltas reported rather than a pass/fail bit; the tolerance decision documented with its rationale; the baseline outputs and their checksums committed as the phase-5 comparison target.

title: P-4: Gap analysis - what is auto-derivable vs what was manually curated
description: The central question for whether mouse can be generated at all. Known manual/curated residue that does NOT fall out of any source file: (1) the 12-entry DROP_EXACT list in refdata/repbase18.05-drop-exact.txt, derived by diffing against the hg38 reference index and unverifiable for mouse; (2) the gene_name->family map for MASTER_FILELIST col4 with its RNU/YRNA/RN7SL/SNORD special cases; (3) the chromosome allowlist pinned to an assembly release; (4) the GENCODE_EXCLUDED_FAMILIES set {RNA5S, RNA5-8S, MTTRNA, MTRNR1, MTRNR2}; (5) MASTER_FILELIST row order. Each is a place where hg38 could be reproduced by fitting to the answer, and where mouse has no answer to fit to. Classify every one as derivable-from-source, derivable-from-rule, or irreducibly-curated, and for the last category state how mouse gets a value and how that value is checked.
acceptance_criteria: Every curated constant enumerated with its derivation and its mouse counterpart or an explicit statement that none exists; each classified derivable vs curated; for each irreducibly-curated item, a stated mouse strategy and validation approach; the analysis flags any hg38 rule that was fit to the reference and therefore carries no evidence for mouse.

title: P-3: Confirm the regeneration source for every human artifact
description: Largely DONE - record it rather than rediscover it. Confirmed sources: repeat consensus = RepBase 18.05 species_specific/homo_sapiens_repbase_fixed_v2.fasta (1,356 records covering 1,224/1,224 index families = 100 percent, verified by header prefix AND canonical sequence digest: 700 byte-exact, 524 matching after IUPAC->N); Gencode v33; UCSC RepeatMasker and simpleRepeat tracks; gtRNAdb tRNA; miRBase gff3; RefSeq NR_046235.1 for RNA45S. Superseded and NOT to be revisited: the RepBase 24.01 two-library method and the RepeatMasker-Edition EMBL parse - the bogus 97.96 percent coverage figure came from missing pseudo.ref/vrtrep.ref/invrep.ref, not from a real library gap. Capture per-source URL, release, download date and checksum.
acceptance_criteria: A source manifest naming, for each of the four artifacts, the exact upstream file, release version and checksum; the superseded RepBase 24.01 path documented as rejected with the reason; every source path verified readable on TSCC.

title: P-2: Document the structure of the four human reference artifacts
description: Structural knowledge exists but is scattered across .forge/stages/2-architect/notes/ (T-03/T-05/T-07/T-09 logs, FIX-PLAN-bowtie2-index.md) and beads memories, in the form of defect narratives rather than a schema. Consolidate into one spec covering, per artifact: column semantics, key space, ordering guarantees, and which consumer reads it. Must capture the two facts already learned the hard way: (a) MASTER_FILELIST row ORDER is behaviorally significant because read_in_filelists assigns priority_n in file order to break equal-score mapping ties, so it must never be sorted; (b) parsed_ucsc_tableformat is order-independent because its consumer keys by transcript id.
acceptance_criteria: One committed schema document covering all four artifacts with column-level semantics and ordering guarantees; each claim cites either the reference file or the consumer code line that depends on it; the hg38 reference files validate against the documented schema.

title: P-1b: Reconstruct provenance of the reference outputs in test-provenance/
description: test-provenance/ has the reference .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv for SE (INV_B.IP.umi.r1.fqTrTr.sorted.fq.barcode1) and PE (204_01_RBFOX2), but configs/, manifests/, scripts/ and reference-metadata/ are ALL EMPTY. Nothing records which inputs, which reference data, which software versions, or which command produced them. That EXAMPLE_SE.* in examples/example_data_for_repeat_mapping_hg38/ is the same dataset as INV_B is currently an INFERENCE from matching unique_distintron counts (2,444,022 vs 2,443,909), not a documented fact. Without this, 'reproduce the reference' is not a well-defined target and phase 5 has no trustworthy baseline to compare against.
acceptance_criteria: Input FASTQ/BAM identity for both reference outputs documented with checksums; the EXAMPLE_SE = INV_B and EXAMPLE_PE = 204_01_RBFOX2 correspondence confirmed or refuted by checksum rather than by read counts; reference-data versions, tool versions and the exact invocation recorded in test-provenance/manifests/; a committed compare script diffs a fresh run against the references and reports per-element deltas.

title: M-8: Define and run the mouse acceptance suite (no gold standard exists)
description: Every hg38 acceptance criterion is 'reproduce the reference file'. Mouse has no reference, so correctness cannot be established the same way and this gap is currently untracked - it is the single largest risk in the mouse effort. Replace reference-diff with cross-artifact consistency checks that would have caught the T-05 and T-09 bugs had they been applied to hg38 without its reference: (a) every MASTER_FILELIST id resolves to an index FASTA header and vice versa; (b) UniqueGenomicElements col4 ids are a subset of MASTER_FILELIST ids; (c) no header carries a ::coords suffix; (d) no family appears in both the repeat and Gencode portions; (e) per-source row counts and the repeat/Gencode/tRNA/miRNA/simplerepeat proportions fall in the same range as hg38; (f) the provenance sidecar covers 100% of emitted repeat families. Implement as a script so mm10 and mm39 are both checked and it can be re-run after any regeneration.
acceptance_criteria: A committed mouse validation script runs all six checks over an assembly directory and exits non-zero on failure; it PASSES on hg38 when pointed at the reference set (proving the checks have teeth); mm10 and mm39 both pass; results recorded in the refdata changelog.

title: M-6: Regenerate mm10/mm39 UniqueGenomicElements with the fixed T-07 rules
description: UniqueGenomicElements.mm10.bed (275MB) and .mm39.bed (277MB) are dated 2026-05-14, before the T-07 multi-source selection fix landed 2026-07-26. They almost certainly still contain the ~1M over-generated simple-repeat rows that rule 1 excludes entirely (hg38 reference is 208MB / 5.6M rows for comparison). Regeneration needs all five fixed rules, which requires the mouse chrom allowlist (M-2), the mm39 tRNA/miRNA inputs (M-1), and the mouse MASTER_FILELIST (M-4, since the Gencode rule selects from it).
acceptance_criteria: Both mouse BEDs regenerated with the committed generator; zero simple-repeat-derived rows; Gencode rows restricted to the mouse MASTER_FILELIST minus the excluded rRNA/mito families; chromosome allowlist applied with the dropped count logged; per-source row counts recorded and compared to the hg38 profile.

title: M-5: Re-derive the mouse DROP_EXACT set against the mouse MASTER_FILELIST
description: FIX-PLAN 4b caveat: DROP_EXACT is a 12-entry constant derived from hg38, and the mouse transfer (only U7_snRNA_Vertebrata and NR_046235.1 apply) is asserted, not verified. The rule is 'drop from the repeat portion whatever Gencode/MASTER_FILELIST supplies' - once a mouse MASTER_FILELIST exists, any family it supplies from Gencode must be added to the mouse DROP_EXACT set, or those reads get double-counted between the repeat and Gencode portions. The same partition also has to stay consistent with the T-07 Gencode exclusion set (RNA5S, RNA5-8S, MTTRNA, MTRNR1, MTRNR2).
acceptance_criteria: Mouse Gencode-supplied families cross-checked against the mouse RepBase selection; refdata/repbase18.05-drop-exact.txt gains a mouse section (or a mouse-specific file) with the derivation recorded; zero family names appear in both the repeat portion and the Gencode portion of the mouse index; T-05/T-09 rerun if the set changes.

title: M-4: Generate mm10/mm39 MASTER_FILELIST
description: The current mouse MASTER_FILELISTs carry the T-09 bug: col4 holds the Gencode biotype (misc_RNA, Mt_tRNA) where the reference holds the curated family (hg38 reference row: ENST00000383925.1 ENSG00000206652.1 RNU1-1 RNU1 genelists.RNU1). Mouse row counts are also inconsistent between assemblies (mm10 11,036 vs mm39 22,368) - reconcile that as part of this work, since it likely reflects a partial mm10 run rather than a real vM23/vM38 difference. Row ORDER is behaviorally significant (read_in_filelists assigns priority_n in file order, breaking equal-score mapping ties) - do not sort.
acceptance_criteria: mm10 and mm39 MASTER_FILELIST regenerated after T-09; col4 holds families not biotypes; repeat class parsed from the T-05 provenance sidecar; the mm10/mm39 row-count gap is explained; a behavioral test shows priority_n ordering is preserved.

title: M-3: Generate mm10/mm39 bowtie2 index FASTA and index
description: The current mm10 (5,875 seqs) and mm39 (22,357 seqs) index FASTAs are products of the T-05 getfasta bug: 5,874/5,875 and 22,356/22,357 headers carry ::chr:start-end(strand) coordinate suffixes, so every mouse index is invalid. After T-05 lands, regenerate both with --repbase-species-fasta mus_musculus_repbase_u1_fixed_v2.fastq (1,194 records, FASTA content despite the .fastq extension). FIX-PLAN 4b predicts 1,079 repeat families after the selection filter (drop 68 Simple_Repeat + 39 tRNA + 6 rRNA + 2 exact); that number is a PREDICTION with no mouse reference to check it against, so the provenance sidecar and non-zero exit on unresolved families are the only guard.
acceptance_criteria: mm10 and mm39 index FASTAs regenerated; zero headers contain '::'; repeat portion is exactly the RepBase 18.05 mouse selection with a provenance row per family; the realized family count is reported against the 1,079 prediction with any delta explained; bowtie2-inspect --summary exits 0 for both.

title: M-2: Build mm10 and mm39 chromosome allowlists
description: T-07 rule 3 pins RepeatMasker rows to a chromosome allowlist for the assembly release; refdata/hg38.chrom-allowlist.txt exists but there is no mouse equivalent, and generate_unique_genomic_elements.py takes --chrom-allowlist as required. Derive from the assembly release the Gencode/RepeatMasker tracks were built against (mm10.fa.fai, GRCm39.primary_assembly.genome.fa.fai), excluding newer patch/_fix/_alt scaffolds the same way hg38 does.
acceptance_criteria: refdata/mm10.chrom-allowlist.txt and refdata/mm39.chrom-allowlist.txt committed with a header comment naming the assembly release they are pinned to; running generate_unique_genomic_elements.py with each drops only patch/alt scaffolds and the dropped count is logged.

title: M-1: Acquire missing mm39 tRNA and miRNA source inputs

title: T-09: fix generate_master_filelist.py Gencode derivation and row order
description:
## Problem
generate_master_filelist.py writes the Gencode *biotype* into col4 where the reference has the curated repeat/gene FAMILY (misc_RNA/snRNA/snoRNA vs RNU6/YRNA/RN7SL/SNORD). Transcript-id overlap with the reference is only ~42% even after stripping version suffixes. The +/-1% line-count AC passed (26,252 vs 26,422 = 0.9936) while the content was substantially wrong.

## Scope
1. Gencode cols 3-5: col3=gene_name; col4=curated family (strip the copy-number suffix, RNU6-2 -> RNU6; group Y_RNA -> YRNA); col5=genelists.{family}. Needs a gene_name->family map with the RNU/YRNA/RN7SL/SNORD special cases.
2. Repeat cols 4-5: family->class (ALUY -> SINE). NO separate mapping table needed - the class is the middle field of the RepBase 18.05 header (ALUY_SINE1/7SL_Primates), carried in T-05's provenance sidecar. Parse it from there.
3. Row order must match the reference or be validated behaviorally: read_in_filelists (parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_SE.pl:463) assigns priority_n in file order and that priority breaks ties between equal-score mappings. Do NOT sort.

## Dependencies
Needs T-05's repeat family set + provenance sidecar. Blocks regeneration of mm10/mm39 UniqueGenomicElements, whose Gencode rule (T-07) requires a mouse MASTER_FILELIST.

Note: the T-07 Gencode partition (MASTER_FILELIST minus rRNA/mito families) and the T-05 §4b DROP_EXACT set describe the same partition and must stay consistent.
acceptance_criteria: col4 holds repeat/gene families not Gencode biotypes; transcript-id overlap with the hg38 reference is materially above the ~42% baseline with the gap explained; repeat class derived from the 18.05 header via the T-05 provenance sidecar rather than a new table; row order reproduces the reference or a behavioral test shows identical priority_n tie-breaking; a mouse MASTER_FILELIST is produced under the same rules; tests cover the gene_name->family special cases and order preservation.

title: T-05: rewrite generate_bowtie2_index.py on RepBase 18.05 species FASTA
description:
## Problem
generate_bowtie2_index.py runs pybedtools getfasta on every genomic repeat *instance*, producing 26,353 seqs with coordinate-suffixed headers instead of 7,606 with clean names. Wrong unit (instance vs family), wrong header format, wrong source. mm10/mm39 indices are wrong the same way.

## Source (confirmed 2026-07-27)
/tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/genomes/RepBase18.05.fasta/species_specific/homo_sapiens_repbase_fixed_v2.fasta (1,356 records) covers 1,224/1,224 index repeat families = 100%, verified by header prefix AND canonical sequence digest (700 byte-exact, 524 match after IUPAC->N = the .fixed.fa step). Mouse counterpart: mus_musculus_repbase_u1_fixed_v2.fastq (1,194 records, FASTA content).

This supersedes the RepBase 24.01 + RepeatMasker-Edition-EMBL two-library plan: no second library, no EMBL parser, no alias table, no >=99% coverage gate.

## Scope
Replace the repeat portion with a single NAME_CLASS_TAXON FASTA parser + the §4b selection filter + uppercase + IUPAC->N. Strip the ::coords suffix from Gencode headers. New CLI --repbase-species-fasta. Emit the §4a provenance sidecar.

Plan: .forge/stages/2-architect/notes/FIX-PLAN-bowtie2-index.md §2-§4b, §7
acceptance_criteria: Repeat portion sourced only from the RepBase 18.05 species FASTA (no getfasta for repeat families, per FIX-PLAN §4a); hg38 output validates at --min-match 1.0 --max-missing 0 against the reference index via validate_fasta_equivalence.py; selection reproduces 1,356->1,224 exactly; every emitted family has a provenance row and unresolved families exit non-zero; all headers clean (no ::coords); bowtie2-inspect --summary exits 0; mm10/mm39 regenerated with the mouse file under identical provenance rules.

title: Remove genomic-instance fallback from RepBase consensus plan
description:
## Problem
The alias-resolution plan proposes genomic getfasta of a representative RepeatMasker instance when a family is absent from both consensus libraries. A genomic instance is not a family consensus and reintroduces the source error that caused T-05. Hg38 sequence comparison may reject it, but mouse has no gold reference to prevent an arbitrary genomic sequence from entering the index.

## Steps to Reproduce
Read FIX-PLAN-bowtie2-index.md lines 56-60 and compare option (c) with the confirmed diagnosis at lines 9-12 and sequence-source rule at lines 46-50.

## Scope
Restrict repeat-family sequences to authoritative consensus sources and explicit aliases. Treat unresolved families as validation failures or documented omissions instead of substituting genomic instances.
acceptance_criteria: The fix plan and implementation contain no representative-genomic-instance fallback for family consensus; every included repeat family records its consensus source and resolved identifier; unresolved families are reported and cannot silently pass the coverage gate; hg38 validation uses per-header sequence equivalence and mouse generation uses the same provenance rules.
close_reason: FIX-PLAN §4a added: permitted consensus sources are RepBase 24.01 .ref, RM Edition RMRBSeqs.embl, and explicit recorded aliases only; representative-genomic-instance getfasta is prohibited for repeat families. Provenance sidecar (family/source/source_file/resolved_id/alias) required per family; unresolved families go to a sidecar, are omitted from the FASTA, exit non-zero unless acknowledged, and the coverage gate uses the selected-set denominator so omissions cannot hide. Mouse uses identical rules.

title: Complete T-07 per-source selection analysis
description:
## Problem
The revised T-07 plan attributes the 1,370,350-row hg38 excess to Gencode selection alone. Restricting 249,043 Gencode rows to the reference's 4,670 removes only 244,373 rows and leaves 1,125,977 unexplained. The generator also emits all 1,049,715 hg38.simplerepeats rows as trf/trf_dup IDs, while the reference BED contains no such names. A Gencode-only fix cannot reproduce hg38 and gives no defensible mouse selection rule.

## Steps to Reproduce
Compare the documented counts 6,988,833 and 5,618,483. Subtract 249,043 minus 4,670. Count decompressed hg38.simplerepeats.tsv.gz rows and search the reference BED column 4 for trf or trf_dup names.

## Scope
Perform a per-source content comparison for RepeatMasker, simple repeats, tRNA, Gencode, and miRNA; derive selection rules from hg38; apply rules consistently to mm10/mm39.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible per-source generated-vs-reference counts and set differences are recorded; selection rules explain the full hg38 delta rather than only Gencode; generated hg38 BED reaches the agreed content threshold with the existing six-column schema; the same rules are defined for mm10/mm39; tests cover inclusion/exclusion for every source.
close_reason: Per-source diff attributes 100% of the 1,370,350-row delta. Five selection rules derived and implemented; hg38 reproduces at recall .99993 / precision .99991 with the existing 6-column schema (RepeatMasker rows exact). mm10/mm39 rules defined in T-07-per-source-selection.log §4 (mouse Gencode rule blocked on T-09). 19 tests cover inclusion+exclusion for every source.

title: Perl mappers have the same unchecked-bowtie2-pipe defect as 475.16
description:
bin/perl/parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_{SE,PE}.pl open bowtie2 as a read pipe (SE:77, PE:79) and never check the result:
  my $pid = open(BOWTIE, '-|', 'stdbuf -oL bowtie2 ... 2> $bowtie_out');
There is no '|| die' on the open and NO close(BOWTIE) anywhere in either script, so $? is never inspected. When bowtie2 fails to launch, while(<BOWTIE>) sees immediate EOF and the script exits 0 having written a 0-byte Rep.sam. This is the identical defect fixed in the Python mappers under 475.16, and it is what produced the original 0-byte Rep.sam that .forge/debug/causal-chain.json misdiagnosed as a transient fault in May 2026.

NOT FIXED DELIBERATELY, for three reasons:
1. The CWL uses 'baseCommand: [parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_SE.pl]', resolved from PATH. Under 'module load ecliprepmap/1.0.0' that resolves to /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/1.0.0/bin/perl/, NOT this repo's copy - and the two files already differ. Patching the repo copy would not change what any CWL run executes.
2. These scripts are the reference implementation used to validate the Snakemake translation (tests/cwl_baseline/). Modifying them perturbs the baseline that equivalence testing depends on.
3. Fixing the installed module is a separate deployment action outside this repo.

Decide explicitly whether the CWL/Perl path is still supported. If it is, the fix belongs in the installed module and should be: close(BOWTIE) or die, then check $? and exit non-zero. If it is not supported, say so in CLAUDE.md and README, since both currently document it as an entry point.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether the CWL/Perl path remains supported; if supported, the installed module's Perl checks the bowtie2 pipe exit status and the repo copy is resynced; if not, the docs stop presenting it as an entry point.

title: ecliprepmap 1.0.0 example is unrunnable as shipped on TSCC2
description:
Two independent breakages in /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/1.0.0/examples/repeat_mapping_SE.yaml:
1. All 'path:' entries use the pre-TSCC2 '/projects/...' prefix. /projects does not exist on TSCC2, so cwltool cannot stage any input.
2. The four INV_B input files under examples/inputs/ are broken symlinks into /projects/ps-yeolab4/software/eclip/0.7.0/... The targets exist under /tscc/projects/... but the links were never repointed after the TSCC1->TSCC2 migration.

Same likely applies to repeat_mapping_PE.yaml and to the 0.1.0 examples. Anyone following the README today gets a staging failure with no hint that the cause is a stale path prefix.
acceptance_criteria: Both example yamls run unmodified after the fix; symlinks repointed or replaced with real paths under /tscc/projects; PE example checked the same way; README notes the TSCC2 path convention.
notes:
THIRD breakage found 2026-08-10, and it is the one that actually stops the run: the SLURM/toil variant CANNOT use node-local scratch.

eCLIP_repelement_SE (non-singleNode) sets CWLRUNNER=slurm and distributes CWL steps as separate toil_job SLURM allocations. /scratch on TSCC2 is node-local NVMe (/dev/nvme0n1p1, 1.5T). Running with JOB_HOME on /scratch put toil's file store on one node's disk while SLURM scheduled the steps on other nodes, so the staged inputs were unreachable:

  parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_SE.pl:464
    open(F,$fi) || die "no $fi\n"
  -> 'no <staged>/MASTER_FILELIST...wmiRs.list', exit 2, Max memory used 30MiB
  -> cwltool: Did not find output file with glob pattern ['INV_B.IP...Rep.sam']
  -> permanentFail

Confirmed by relaunching with JOB_HOME on /tscc/lustre/ddn/scratch/bay001 (1.7P, shared): the toil jobs then spread across tscc-4-18, tscc-11-57 and tscc-14-46 simultaneously and staging succeeded.

RULE: singleNode variants may use /scratch; the SLURM variants MUST use a shared filesystem (/tscc/lustre/ddn/scratch or /tscc/projects). Worth stating in the README next to the path fixes, since the failure surfaces as a misleading 'no <file>' from a Perl script rather than as a filesystem error.

title: Fix FASTA normalization and per-header hash validation
description:
## Problem
The sequence-validation AWK sketch replaces uppercase IUPAC symbols before uppercasing, so lowercase ambiguity codes such as rymk remain RYMK rather than NNNN. It also joins full sequences while describing the operation as a per-header hash comparison.

## Steps to Reproduce
Pipe a FASTA record containing lowercase rymk through the norm function in FIX-PLAN-bowtie2-index.md lines 90-93. The output sequence is RYMK instead of NNNN.

## Scope
Provide an executable, memory-conscious validator that canonicalizes FASTA records consistently and compares actual per-header digests.
acceptance_criteria: Normalization uppercases before converting all non-ACGT ambiguity codes required by policy to N; multiline and lowercase FASTA inputs are covered by tests; duplicate headers fail validation; per-header cryptographic hashes are compared; the validator reports shared, missing, extra, matching, and mismatching header counts and enforces the documented threshold.
close_reason: Replaced the broken AWK sketch with bin/python/refdata_generation/validate_fasta_equivalence.py: uppercases before mapping every non-ACGT byte to N (fixes lowercase rymk -> RYMK), per-header SHA-256 compared, duplicate headers exit 2, streams records so memory is O(headers). Reports new/reference/shared/missing/extra/matching/mismatching and enforces --min-match and --max-missing. 18 tests incl. multiline+lowercase FASTA, all IUPAC codes, MER5A same-header-different-sequence. Verified on the real 7,606-seq reference index.

Root cause of se_full/pe_full '#READINFO RepFamilyReads 0 0': bowtie2 was NOT ON PATH for those runs. results/se_full/barcode1/mapped/rep.sam.bowtieout (67 bytes, present on disk) says 'stdbuf: failed to run command bowtie2: No such file or directory', identical in all 5 full-run samples; the small runs' bowtieout files have real alignment summaries. The full runs were launched without --use-conda. NOT scale-dependent - my earlier 'deterministic, scale-dependent' claim was WRONG, size only correlated because full and small runs were launched differently.

THE REAL DEFECT was silent failure: map_repetitive_elements_{se,pe}.py called proc.wait() and discarded the exit code, then wrote '.done' and exited 0. stdbuf exits 127; the pipe reader read immediate EOF as a successful zero-alignment run, and downstream splitbam/dedup/combine consumed the empty rep.sam. That is why it looked like a transient bowtie2 fault for months (.forge/debug/causal-chain.json).

FIXED on branch fix/bowtie2-silent-failure: check_bowtie_exit() in both mappers surfaces bowtie2 stderr and exits non-zero without writing '.done'. 4 regression tests in tests/workflow_scripts/ fail pre-fix, pass post-fix. se_small re-run unchanged (1784/0.80907, 1162/0.55946, RNA28S 703) so the success path is intact.
